Response families for stem counts and basal area

magCompFamilies.Rd

Constructs a response family for magComp. Both families model negative-binomial totals and multinomial category allocation. Either component can be fitted alone by setting the other formula to NULL.

Usage

fixedAreaStems()

pointBasalArea()

Details

fixedAreaStems() uses fixed-area plot counts. Its magnitude is stem density \(M_i\), so the expected plot total is \(a_i M_i\) for area \(a_i\). Supply a fixedArea design when preparing data.

pointBasalArea() uses horizontal point-sampling in-tree tallies. Its magnitude is basal area per unit area \(M_i^{BA}\), so the expected tally is \(M_i^{BA}/\mathrm{BAF}_i\). Supply a pointSampling design. Tree-factor-expanded stem counts or other attributes are not fitted responses.

Negative-binomial size is positive and finite. Both families estimate it by default under a Gamma(shape = 1, rate = 0.01) prior when the magnitude formula has no latent process terms. With magnitude iid or spatial terms, size is fixed at control$nb_size (default 1000). Use magCompPriors to change the prior or explicitly fix size. Large sizes approximate a Poisson model; the sampler does not fit an exact Poisson model.

Both families support expected fitted values and predictions, as well as replicate or new observations from the fitted likelihood. Point-sampling count outputs are in-tree tallies, with mean \(M_i^{BA}/\mathrm{BAF}_i\); observation magnitude multiplies the tally by BAF to give a sampled basal-area estimate. Composition-only models simulate allocations conditional on observed or supplied totals under either family, including for posterior predictive checks. Plot area or BAF is unnecessary for composition-only fitting and probabilities; it is needed for conditional density. standSummary aggregates density or magnitude samples under either family using represented land areas.

Value

A magCompFamily object with likelihood equal to "negative_binomial_multinomial".

See also

magCompData, magCompControl, magCompPriors; the technical guide's Fixed-area count model and Point-sampling basal area sections in magComp-package.
